glosses: to tear, to tear apart, to rip, to rip apart (to cause something to fall violently into pieces or to break off many fragments from it by using one's teeth or other part of the body, or a sharp object)
to loot (to steal by violent means from some whole or some place in succession so many things that nothing remains)
to overwhelm (to defeat in a decisive manner)
to tear apart, to rip apart (to become the cause of very unpleasant physical sensations or psychological trauma)

to get torn, to get torn apart, to get ripped, to get ripped apart (to fall violently into pieces or to break off into many fragments by using one's teeth or other part of the body, or a sharp object)

to tear each other, to tear each other apart, to rip each other, to rip each other apart (to cause each other to fall violently into pieces or to break off into many fragments by using teeth or other part of the body, or a sharp object)
to overwhelm each other (to defeat each other in a decisive manner)
